In RPG Maker MV one of the coolest base additions for a player in my opinion was the game remembering what your previous command was and blowing through them very quickly when your selection button was held.
Is there a script version of this for VXA?
If so can I have it!
-Axel

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
Something like this?
Ruby:
#==============================================================================
# Game_Battler
#==============================================================================
class Game_Battler
  attr_accessor :last_battle_command
end #Game_Battler

#==============================================================================
# Window_ActorCommand
#==============================================================================
class Window_ActorCommand < Window_Command
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # overide method: call_ok_handler
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def call_ok_handler
    @actor.last_battle_command = current_symbol if handle?(current_symbol)
    super
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # override method: activate
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def activate
    r = super
    select_last
    return r
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # new method: select_last
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def select_last
    select(0)
    return unless @actor
    cmd = @actor.last_battle_command
    select_symbol(cmd) if cmd
    if cmd == :skill
      skill = @actor.last_skill.object
      select_ext(skill.stype_id) if skill
    end
  end
end #Window_ActorCommand
The
select_last
code is basically the same as the method in MV's version.

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
I wrote a base script to have your automash.
You can replace the code from
self.enabled?
or just set the value of
SWITCH_ID
to fit your automash option.
Ruby:
#==============================================================================
# AutoMash
#==============================================================================
module AutoMash
  #put a value above 0 to have a switch allow the automash when true
  SWITCH_ID = 0 
  
  def self.enabled?(key)
    SWITCH_ID > 0 ? $game_switches[SWITCH_ID] : true
  end
end #AutoMash

#==============================================================================
# Window_Selectable
#==============================================================================
class Window_Selectable < Window_Base
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # overwrite method: process_handling
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def process_handling
    return unless open? && active
    return process_ok       if ok_enabled?        && check_input(:C)
    return process_cancel   if cancel_enabled?    && check_input(:B)
    return process_pagedown if handle?(:pagedown) && check_input(:R)
    return process_pageup   if handle?(:pageup)   && check_input(:L)
  end
  
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # new method: check_input -> allow to switch between repeat or trigger based
  # on module option
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def check_input(key)
    AutoMash.enabled?(key) ? Input.repeat?(key) : Input.trigger?(key)
  end
end #Window_Selectable

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
You can replace the call to
select_last
in the
activate
method to have a switch requirement:
Ruby:
module MemoryBattleCommand
  SWITCH_ID = 0
 
  def self.enabled?
    SWITCH_ID <= 0 || $game_switches[SWITCH_ID]
  end
end #MemoryBattleCommand

#==============================================================================
# Game_Battler
#==============================================================================
class Game_Battler
  attr_accessor :last_battle_command
end #Game_Battler

#==============================================================================
# Window_ActorCommand
#==============================================================================
class Window_ActorCommand < Window_Command
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # overide method: call_ok_handler
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def call_ok_handler
    @actor.last_battle_command = current_symbol if handle?(current_symbol)
    super
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # override method: activate
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def activate
    r = super
    select_last if MemoryBattleCommand.enabled?
    return r
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # new method: select_last
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def select_last
    select(0)
    return unless @actor
    cmd = @actor.last_battle_command
    select_symbol(cmd) if cmd
    if cmd == :skill
      skill = @actor.last_skill.object
      select_ext(skill.stype_id) if skill
    end
  end
end #Window_ActorCommand

Did want to come back to add on. At least for me, the game would lag behind if the auto mashed button was held during Actor/Battler Actions so I added in something of a modification to hopefully help, my pc is very low end so, it was something I think I should add.
Code:
def check_input(key)
  AutoMash.enabled?(key) ? Input.repeat?(key) : Input.trigger?(key) unless BattleManager.in_turn?
end
